page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6e-c12g1.12xlarge is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance powered by 24 physical cores and 48 virtual CPUs of Intel Xeon Platinum 8163 processors operating at 2.5 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The server features dedicated CPU resource allocation supported by 33 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction set support. System memory totals 368 GB, offering 7.67 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration hardware consists of four NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs delivering 128 GB of aggregate VRAM. The instance operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps and contains no local SSD storage.

In synthetic benchmark evaluations, single-core processing performance falls into the lower quartile, reflected in a stress-ng single-core score of 1110.4 and lower single-threaded compression throughput. Conversely, multi-core performance scales into average benchmark tiers, reaching 35520.27 in stress-ng multi-core testing and 147.7 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Cached memory bandwidth achieves 1975.99 GB/sec, while uncached large-block read and write bandwidths measure 98.85 GB/sec and 47.39 GB/sec. Concurrent execution benchmarks demonstrate high throughput, including 33.18 million Redis SET operations per second and 23.02 GB/sec in static web serving testing.

The instance delivers strong resource density by pairing multi-GPU hardware acceleration with substantial memory allocation, making it cost effective for heavily parallelized workloads rather than single-threaded CPU routines. The absence of local disk storage mandates reliance on external network storage solutions. This hardware profile is appropriate for deep learning model training, multi-GPU inference pipelines, high-throughput scientific simulations, and large-scale parallel data analytics.

Hardware acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs equipped with an aggregate 128 GB of VRAM. The instance provides a 16 Gbps baseline network interface and relies entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations indicate modest single-core execution alongside solid multi-core performance, achieving 35520.27 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 33.18 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 1975.99 GB/sec for small cached blocks. By combining dedicated multi-core CPU capacity with four dedicated graphics processing units, this instance provides balanced hardware density suited for parallel computational tasks, artificial intelligence model training, multi-GPU inference pipelines, and scientific data processing.
